indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.1.1.1 Understand the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Classify animals into insects, birds, mammals and reptiles

skills.description: Recognise the main observable features of insects, birds, mammals and reptiles (body covering, limbs, young ones, where they live).
Place a named Ghanaian animal into the correct group: insect, bird, mammal or reptile.
Give a simple reason for a classification using an observable feature, not just the animal's name.
Identify whether an animal is an example or non-example of a named group.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: All animals that fly are birds.
All small crawling animals are insects.
Mammals are only large land animals.
Reptiles are insects because they crawl.

questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of all insects?
options: They feed their young with milk.
They have scales on their body.
hints: Think about how many legs a cockroach or housefly has.
Count the legs on an ant.
questions.explanation: Insects have six legs. Feathers belong to birds, milk-feeding belongs to mammals, and scales belong to reptiles.
questions.misconception: Some learners think any small crawling animal is an insect.

questions.stem: A dog is best classified as which of these?
hints: Think about how a dog's body is covered.
Does a dog feed its puppies with milk?
questions.explanation: A dog has hair, gives birth to live young, and feeds its puppies with milk. These are features of mammals.
questions.misconception: Some learners think only wild animals are mammals.

questions.stem: A butterfly belongs to which group of animals?
hints: How many legs does a butterfly have?
Look at the body of a butterfly — is it in three parts?
questions.explanation: A butterfly has six legs and a body divided into three parts. These are features of insects.
questions.misconception: Some learners think butterflies are birds because they have wings.

questions.stem: Which group of animals has feathers covering their bodies?
hints: Think about the animals you see in a poultry farm.
What covers the body of a hen?
questions.explanation: Birds are the only group of animals among these that have feathers.
questions.misconception: Some learners think all flying animals have feathers.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is a reptile?
hints: Reptiles have dry skin covered with scales.
Think of an animal that crawls on its belly.
questions.explanation: A snake has dry, scaly skin and crawls on its belly. It is a reptile.
questions.misconception: Some learners think all crawling animals are insects.

questions.stem: A parrot is best classified as which of these?
hints: Think about what covers a parrot's body.
Parrots have beaks and wings.
questions.explanation: A parrot has feathers, wings, and a beak. It is a bird.
questions.misconception: Some learners think parrots are mammals because they can talk.

questions.stem: A snake belongs to which group of animals?
hints: What covers the body of a snake?
Does a snake have legs?
questions.explanation: A snake has dry, scaly skin and no legs. These features show it is a reptile.
questions.misconception: Some learners think snakes are insects because they crawl.

questions.stem: Why is a bat grouped as a mammal and not a bird, even though it flies?
options: It has feathers on its body.
It has six legs and a three-part body.
It has hair and feeds its young with milk.
It has dry scales on its skin.
hints: Look at what covers a bat's body.
Think about how a bat feeds its babies.
questions.explanation: A bat has hair on its body and feeds its young with milk. These are mammal features. Flying alone does not make an animal a bird.
questions.misconception: All animals that fly are birds.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is NOT a mammal?
hints: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young with milk.
Which of these animals has scales?
questions.explanation: A crocodile has scales and lays eggs. It is a reptile, not a mammal. The cow, goat and dog all have hair and feed their young with milk.
questions.misconception: Some learners think all four-legged animals are mammals.

questions.stem: Which group of animals has dry skin covered with scales?
hints: Think of the skin of a lizard.
What covers a crocodile's body?
questions.explanation: Reptiles such as lizards, snakes, and crocodiles have dry, scaly skin.
questions.misconception: Some learners think fish and reptiles are the same because both have scales.

questions.stem: A grasscutter belongs to which group of animals?
hints: Does a grasscutter have hair or fur?
Does it feed its young with milk?
questions.explanation: A grasscutter has fur and feeds its young with milk. It is a mammal.
questions.misconception: Some learners think grasscutters are reptiles because they live in holes.

questions.stem: A learner says a spider is an insect because it has many legs. What is the best correction?
options: A spider is not an insect because it has eight legs, not six.
A spider is a mammal because it has hair.
A spider is a reptile because it has scales.
A spider is a bird because it can climb trees.
hints: Count the legs on a spider.
How many legs do insects have?
questions.explanation: Insects have six legs. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect.
questions.misconception: Spiders are insects.

questions.stem: Give one reason why a lizard is classified as a reptile.
answer: it has dry skin covered with scales
hints: Think about the skin of a lizard.
Does a lizard have feathers or scales?
questions.explanation: A lizard has dry skin covered with scales. This is a feature of reptiles.
questions.misconception: Some learners think lizards are insects because they crawl.

questions.stem: Why is a whale classified as a mammal and not a fish?
options: It lives in water and has fins.
It has scales and lays eggs.
It breathes air and feeds its young with milk.
hints: Think about how a whale breathes.
Does a whale feed its baby with milk?
questions.explanation: A whale breathes air and feeds its young with milk. These are mammal features, even though it lives in water.
questions.misconception: All animals that live in water are fish.

questions.stem: Name two mammals that live in water.
hints: Think of large animals in the sea that breathe air.
They feed their babies with milk.
questions.explanation: Whales and dolphins are mammals that live in water. They breathe air and feed their young with milk.
questions.misconception: All animals in water are fish.

questions.stem: A millipede has many legs. Is it an insect? Explain your answer.
answer: no, it has more than six legs
no, it is not an insect because it has many legs, not six
hints: How many legs does an insect have?
Count the legs on a millipede — is it six?
questions.explanation: A millipede is not an insect because it has many more than six legs. Insects have exactly six legs.
questions.misconception: All small crawling animals are insects.

questions.stem: State one difference between birds and reptiles.
answer: birds have feathers but reptiles have scales
birds have feathers, reptiles have scales
birds have feathers and reptiles do not
hints: What covers the body of a bird?
What covers the body of a reptile?
questions.explanation: Birds have feathers on their bodies, while reptiles have dry scales.
questions.misconception: Some learners think all animals with wings are birds.

questions.stem: A learner finds a small animal with six legs, wings, and a body in three parts. Which group does it belong to and why?
options: Insect, because it has six legs and a three-part body.
hints: Count the legs.
How many body parts does it have?
questions.explanation: Six legs and a body in three parts are insect features. Wings alone are not enough to make it a bird because it has no feathers.
questions.misconception: All animals that fly are birds.

questions.stem: A friend says, 'All animals that fly are birds.' Name two flying animals that are NOT birds and state their groups.
answer: butterfly is an insect and bat is a mammal
bat is a mammal, butterfly is an insect
hints: Think of an animal that flies at night and has fur.
Think of an insect with colourful wings.
questions.explanation: A bat is a mammal that flies, and a butterfly is an insect that flies. Flying alone does not make an animal a bird.
questions.misconception: All animals that fly are birds.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly explains why a cow is a mammal?
options: It has four legs and lives on land.
It eats grass and chews cud.
It has a tail and horns.
It has hair, gives birth to live young, and feeds its calf with milk.
hints: What covers a cow's body?
How does a cow feed its calf?
questions.explanation: A cow has hair, gives birth to live young, and feeds its calf with milk. These are the key features of mammals.
questions.misconception: All four-legged animals are mammals.
